year_filter.rule: The preferred Version must have a publisher, proceedings, repository, or preprint date inside the interval. Earlier Preprints are retained only as Versions of a qualifying 2026 Work.

lane_title: Prompt Engineering, prompt-based debiasing and fairness evaluation in socially consequential settings
scope: Primary empirical publications on prompt engineering, prompt-based debiasing, persona or role prompting, fairness instructions, prompt-population evaluation, and systematic tests of their effectiveness or failure. Eligible Works require a substantive gender, social-bias, inequality, diversity, fairness, stigma, or protected-group dimension and direct or reasoned transfer to social work, human services, mental health, health care, education, counselling, child welfare, hiring, or person-level decisions.

searched_sources: ACL Anthology 2026 proceedings and workshop volumes
ICLR 2026 official proceedings and conference dates
deduplication_sources: corpus/deep-research/round2/Codex Websearch/raw (other available lane files at validation time)

saturation.basis: Conference-specific, publisher-specific, repository-specific, title-chain, DOI, application-domain, and protected-attribute searches converged. The final expansion round mostly returned already identified Works, prompt use without a social-bias question, static audits without prompt comparison, or non-prompt training and activation interventions.

last_round_yield.description: The final targeted searches added the medRxiv clinical-stigma prompt experiment and the LT-EDI use-case-specific prompt framework; further hits were exclusions or duplicates.

limitations: No subscription bibliographic index such as Scopus or Web of Science was queried.
Some publisher pages expose metadata and abstracts but restrict the Version of Record full text.
For several 2026 proceedings papers no earlier public Preprint was found; their Version arrays therefore contain only the proceedings Version.
Preprints remain unreviewed even when their empirical scope is strong.

candidates.title: Same Prompt, Different Care? Evaluating Inequities in AI-Generated Mental Health Support for Immigrant Communities
candidates.venue: Journal of the Society for Social Work and Research

preferred_version.reason: Dated journal publication inside the search window.

peer_review_evidence.basis: The publisher and Crossref identify a journal article, but no item-specific review history was located.

eligibility.technical: Controlled comparison of equivalent prompts across LLM-generated mental-health support.
eligibility.social: Direct social-work, immigrant-community, multilingual inequity, and mental-health support setting.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Comparative multilingual prompt audit across ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini.
eligibility.rationale: Both review dimensions are direct and the application is a core Human Services setting.

notes: Publisher access was restricted at the cutoff date.

candidates.title: Multi-Persona Thinking for Bias Mitigation in Large Language Models
candidates.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026

preferred_version.reason: Peer-reviewed proceedings Version supersedes the Preprint.

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official Findings of ACL 2026 proceedings record.

eligibility.technical: Inference-time deliberation among contrasting male, female, and neutral personas identifies and corrects biased judgments.
eligibility.social: Direct gender and social-stereotype mitigation.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Multi-model comparison on two established bias benchmarks.
eligibility.rationale: Direct empirical prompt intervention with a protected-group fairness outcome.

candidates.title: Mitigating medical bias in large language models by prompt engineering: an empirical study of effectiveness and trade-offs
candidates.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A

peer_review_evidence.basis: Royal Society journal publication; item-specific review history was not located.

eligibility.technical: Five prompt strategies are compared across five LLMs for fairness, accuracy, and inference cost.
eligibility.social: Direct medical fairness and sensitive-group patient-safety context.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Controlled benchmark experiment; chain-of-thought reduces the average group gap but no strategy is universally effective.
eligibility.rationale: Direct, peer-published prompt mitigation in a high-stakes service domain.

notes: The DOI contains 2025, but the documented publication date is 2026-07-16.

candidates.title: Patient Cognitive Bias in Large Language Model-Supported Health Consultations: Simulation-Based Comparative Study

peer_review_evidence.basis: JMIR records submission, acceptance on 2026-05-04, and journal publication.

eligibility.technical: Three prompt mitigations are tested in three-round consultations under patient cognitive-bias cues.
eligibility.social: Direct patient-facing health consultation and person-level decision support.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: 1,273 MedQA cases, six LLMs, four temperatures; prompt effects are modest and inconsistent.
eligibility.rationale: Strong systematic countercheck of prompt mitigation in an interactive Human Services setting.

candidates.title: ELEPHANT: Measuring and understanding social sycophancy in LLMs

preferred_version.reason: Official ICLR 2026 proceedings Version; main conference began 2026-04-23.

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official ICLR 2026 conference proceedings record.

eligibility.technical: Introduces a social-sycophancy benchmark and tests prompting and steering mitigations.
eligibility.social: Directly concerns advice, moral conflict, user affirmation, and relational harm relevant to counselling and support interactions.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Eleven-model audit; 45-point human-model preservation gap and 48% two-sided affirmation under perspective prompts.
eligibility.rationale: High-value prompt-effect study for counselling-like interactions.

notes: The mitigation methods require trade-off evaluation because reduced sycophancy may affect perceived supportiveness.

candidates.title: Persona-Assigned Large Language Models Exhibit Human-Like Motivated Reasoning
candidates.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official Findings of ACL 2026 record.

eligibility.technical: Eight personas across political and sociodemographic attributes are tested with conventional prompt-debiasing methods.
eligibility.social: Identity-congruent misinformation and scientific-evidence judgments transfer to education, public health, and counselling.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Eight LLMs and two tasks derived from human-subject studies; prompt debiasing is largely ineffective.
eligibility.rationale: Strong counter-evidence on persona and fairness prompting.

candidates.title: I Am Not Them: Persistent Outgroup Bias in Large Language Models Arising from Social Identity Persona Setting
candidates.venue: Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference

preferred_version.reason: Official LREC 2026 Version with an additional author and final title.

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official LREC 2026 proceedings record.

eligibility.technical: Persona prompts induce ingroup and outgroup bias; an identity-switch prompt is tested as mitigation.
eligibility.social: Validated across political and gender domains with explicit prejudice and discrimination framing.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Controlled persona intervention neutralizes pre-existing group bias in the reported experiments.
eligibility.rationale: Direct prompt-based social-bias mechanism and mitigation.

notes: The two earlier Preprints have variant titles and author lists; they are treated as a Version chain, not separate Works.

candidates.title: Mitigating Cultural Bias in LLMs via Multi-Agent Cultural Debate
candidates.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official Findings of ACL 2026 record.

eligibility.technical: Training-free multi-agent debate assigns explicit cultural personas and tests language prompting as a failed mitigation baseline.
eligibility.social: Western-, East Asian-, and Arabic-cultural bias is directly measured.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: CEBiasBench and CAMeL experiments; reported no-bias rates improve over the GPT-4o baseline.
eligibility.rationale: Strong culturally responsive prompting evidence transferable to immigrant and cross-cultural services.

candidates.title: InsideOut: Measuring and Mitigating Insider–Outsider Bias in Interview Script Generation
candidates.venue: 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official ACL 2026 main-conference proceedings record.

eligibility.technical: Compares a fairness-instruction prompt with three fairness-agent pipelines in an interview-script task.
eligibility.social: Measures Americentric insider-outsider positioning across ten cultures.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: 4,000 prompts and five LLMs; agent methods reduce cultural-alignment gaps by up to 89.70% in reported model-method pairs.
eligibility.rationale: Direct prompt and agent mitigation for culturally situated interviewing, transferable to assessment and service encounters.

candidates.title: Addressing benchmarking gaps in large language models for health and medicine with dynamic red-teaming

peer_review_evidence.basis: Nature Health research-article publication; received and accepted dates are displayed, but review reports were not located.

eligibility.technical: Dynamic agents mutate prompts and escalate attacks across robustness, privacy, bias-fairness, and hallucination axes.
eligibility.social: Bias tests alter sociodemographic identity, language, emotion, and cognitive cues in health and clinical decisions.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Fifteen LLMs, more than 100,000 scored microtasks, and over 100 million adversarial-dialogue tokens; identity or cognitive cues alter recommendations in 81% of tests.
eligibility.rationale: Strong prompt-evaluation evidence in a high-stakes health setting.

notes: The intervention is an auditing/red-teaming framework rather than a user-facing debiasing prompt.

candidates.title: Large language models exhibit stigmatizing behaviour in contextual judgements of health conditions

peer_review_evidence.basis: Nature Health research-article publication; item-specific review reports were not located.

eligibility.technical: Contrasts explicit stigma scales with contextual prompt judgments and derives transferable prompting strategies from model reasoning.
eligibility.social: Direct mental-health, HIV, hepatitis-B, stigma, multilingual, and clinical-deployment relevance.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Six LLMs, 51 scenarios, 61,200 model decisions; derived prompt strategies are associated with lower stigma-congruent responses across languages and scenarios.
eligibility.rationale: Direct social-bias prompt mitigation in health and mental-health contexts.

duplicate_check.notes: Previously recorded as an exclusion; the publisher abstract now establishes evaluated prompting strategies, so this lane upgrades it to Tier A.

notes: The Version of Record full text was restricted; the abstract supplies the prompt-strategy result.

candidates.title: BiasFreeBench: a Benchmark for Mitigating Bias in Large Language Model Responses

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official ICLR 2026 conference-paper record and OpenReview identifier.

eligibility.technical: Compares four prompt-based and four training-based debiasing methods.
eligibility.social: Nine social-bias types include gender, age, disability, and socioeconomic status.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Seven LLMs on BBQ and FairMT-Bench; prompt methods are generally stronger, with method-model trade-offs.
eligibility.rationale: A broad empirical comparison directly answering prompt-mitigation effectiveness.

notes: Application transfer is general rather than tied to one Human Services workflow.

candidates.title: No Free Lunch in Language Model Bias Mitigation? Targeted Bias Reduction Can Exacerbate Unmitigated LLM Biases

peer_review_evidence.basis: Publisher journal record and public review-report page.

eligibility.technical: Systematically tests four mitigation techniques, including prompt debiasing, for on-target effects and spillover harms.
eligibility.social: Gender, race, religion, and profession biases are jointly evaluated.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: 160 interventions and 640 evaluations across ten models; significant spillover harm exceeds significant on-target gains in the reported counts.
eligibility.rationale: Strong countercheck of isolated bias-mitigation claims and directly relevant to multi-axis fairness.

notes: Prompt debiasing is one of four evaluated interventions.

candidates.title: Gender Bias in LLM Hiring Decisions: Evidence from a Japanese Context and Evaluation of Mitigation Strategies

preferred_version.reason: Only public Version found by the cutoff.

peer_review_evidence.basis: arXiv Preprint; no accepted Version located.

eligibility.technical: Compares baseline, gender-neutrality instruction, and privacy-filter prompts.
eligibility.social: Direct gender fairness in Japanese hiring decisions.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: 60 resumes, 12 name pairs, five LLMs, and 43,200 API calls; the fairness instruction is ineffective while name removal changes behavior and refusals.
eligibility.rationale: Strong topic fit, retained as Tier B because evidence is Preprint-only.

candidates.title: Can Fairness Be Prompted? Prompt-Based Debiasing Strategies in High-Stakes Recommendations

peer_review_evidence.basis: arXiv Preprint only.

eligibility.technical: Tests three bias-aware prompting strategies across models and recommendation templates.
eligibility.social: Employment and news recommendations use gender and age attributes.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Three LLMs, four templates, nine sensitive-attribute values, and two recommendation datasets; fairness gains can overpromote groups.
eligibility.rationale: Direct high-stakes prompt mitigation, but unreviewed.

candidates.title: Bring Your Own Prompts: Use-Case-Specific Bias and Fairness Evaluation for LLMs
candidates.venue: Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official ACL Anthology workshop record; item-specific review details were not located.

eligibility.technical: Maps use cases and prompt populations to fairness metrics and supplies an open evaluation library.
eligibility.social: Covers toxicity, stereotyping, counterfactual unfairness, protected attributes, and allocational harms.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Five LLMs and five prompt populations show benchmark-to-deployment fairness instability.
eligibility.rationale: Highly relevant evaluation method, but application transfer remains generic and venue is a workshop.

candidates.title: SPAGBias: Uncovering and Tracing Structured Spatial Gender Bias in Large Language Models
candidates.venue: 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official ACL 2026 main-conference record.

eligibility.technical: A prompt library and three diagnostic layers test how prompt design, temperature, and scale alter bias expression.
eligibility.social: Direct spatial gender bias with downstream urban-planning and health-access implications.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Six models, 62 urban micro-spaces, repeated sampling, token asymmetry, and narrative analysis.
eligibility.rationale: Strong gender audit; retained as Tier B because no prompt mitigation is experimentally established.

candidates.title: Can Persona-Prompted LLMs Emulate Subgroup Values? An Empirical Analysis of Generalisability and Fairness in Cultural Alignment
candidates.venue: 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official ACL 2026 main-conference record.

eligibility.technical: Tests persona prompts for subgroup-value emulation and compares fine-tuning.
eligibility.social: Finds systematic preference for young, male, Chinese, and Christian personas in Singaporean value alignment.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: About 20,000 World Values Survey-based samples; GPT-4.1 reaches 57.4% subgroup modal preference, while fine-tuning improves averages but widens disparities.
eligibility.rationale: Strong persona-fairness evidence, but the mitigation is principally fine-tuning.

candidates.title: Analysing LLM Persona Generation and Fairness Interpretation in Polarised Geopolitical Contexts

preferred_version.reason: ACL Anthology identifies v2 as the corrected Version.

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official EACL Student Research Workshop record.

eligibility.technical: Tests explicit fairness instructions in persona generation and compares rationales with outcomes.
eligibility.social: Palestinian and Israeli identities, socioeconomic status, occupation, and non-binary gender inference are directly analyzed.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Five LLMs and 640 conditions; fairness language in reasoning does not consistently translate to fair output distributions.
eligibility.rationale: Strong prompt-failure evidence, but Student Research Workshop status supports Tier B.

candidates.title: ‘A Woman is More Culturally Knowledgeable than A Man?’: The Effect of Personas on Cultural Norm Interpretation in LLMs

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official ACL Anthology workshop record.

eligibility.technical: Evaluates how persona prompting changes cultural-norm interpretation.
eligibility.social: Direct gender and cultural stereotype question across 34 personas.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Four LLMs, 34 personas, and 12 persona categories.
eligibility.rationale: Direct persona-gender audit, but no mitigation and a workshop venue.

candidates.title: Equilibrium Dynamics and Mitigation of Gender Bias in Synthetically Generated Data
candidates.venue: Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official ACL Anthology workshop record.

eligibility.technical: Recursive prompting is tested across three synthetic-data generations and four mitigations.
eligibility.social: Direct gender-bias amplification and mitigation.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Three initial bias levels; contrastive gender-swapping reduces downstream bias strongly while embedding metrics disagree.
eligibility.rationale: Useful prompt-generation countercheck, but downstream Human Services transfer is indirect and venue is a workshop.

candidates.title: Large Language Models Are Still Misled by Simple Bias Ensembles
candidates.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official Findings of ACL 2026 record.

eligibility.technical: A multi-bias benchmark systematically retests current debiasing methods under compounded prompt cues.
eligibility.social: Includes occupation-gender bias and explicitly motivates clinical diagnosis and legal-document analysis.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Controlled multi-bias benchmark shows rapid degradation and poor performance of existing debiasing methods.
eligibility.rationale: Strong robustness evidence, but the abstract does not isolate a prompt-specific mitigation contribution.

candidates.title: Controlling Distributional Bias in Multi-Round LLM Generation via KL-Optimized Fine-Tuning
candidates.venue: 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official ACL 2026 main-conference record.

eligibility.technical: Repeated-prompt generation tests prompt engineering and DPO as unsuccessful distribution-control baselines.
eligibility.social: Gender, race, sentiment, occupation, and educational-text representation are direct protected-attribute contexts.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Six datasets show prompt engineering does not reliably control output distributions; the successful method is fine-tuning.
eligibility.rationale: Retained as a negative prompt-effect finding; main intervention is outside prompt scope.

duplicate_check.notes: Previously recorded as an exclusion; the current broader countercheck scope supports Tier B.

candidates.title: Prompt Engineering for Social Workers
candidates.venue: Social Work Practice and Artificial Intelligence for the Common Good

peer_review_evidence.basis: Routledge chapter publication; chapter-specific peer review was not established.

eligibility.technical: Introduces a P.I.C.O. prompt framework intended to reduce bias, protect privacy, and support iterative verification.
eligibility.social: Directly addressed to social workers and social-work practice.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Not established from accessible publisher metadata.
eligibility.rationale: Direct domain and prompt fit, but empirical contribution and chapter review status require full-text screening.

candidates.title: AI-Generated Images of Social Workers in Healthcare and Implications for Professional Identity

peer_review_evidence.basis: Australian Social Work journal article; item-specific review history not displayed.

eligibility.technical: Uses refined prompts with two generative-image systems and critically analyzes outputs.
eligibility.social: Direct social-work professional identity, gender norms, racial representation, patient invisibility, and biomedical hierarchy.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Critical discourse analysis of 16 generated images from two platforms.
eligibility.rationale: Direct social-work and prompt-bias evidence, but multimodal image generation and no mitigation comparison place it in Tier B.

candidates.title: Large Language Models Generate Stigmatizing Language During Reasoning Over Real-World Clinical Data

preferred_version.reason: Latest public Preprint Version before the cutoff.

peer_review_evidence.basis: medRxiv explicitly states that the article has not been certified by peer review.

eligibility.technical: Tests prompt engineering as a destigmatizing intervention in LLM reasoning traces.
eligibility.social: Direct clinical documentation, stigma, health-equity, and patient-safety relevance.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: 107 LLMs, 35 real-world clinical tasks, and 3,745 model-task pairs; prompt engineering reduces stigma by up to 91.91% in reported cases without lowering task performance.
eligibility.rationale: Strong empirical prompt mitigation, retained as Tier B because it is an unreviewed medical Preprint.

notes: v2 updates Figure 4C, results analysis, and the Discussion relative to v1.

candidates.title: Exploring attribution bias in LLMs: Social influences and prompt-based mitigation

peer_review_evidence.basis: Technology in Society journal article; item-specific review history not located.

eligibility.technical: Controlled prompt interventions reduce attributional extremity.
eligibility.social: Manipulates gender, age, education, region, perspective, and event valence, with education, law, and healthcare transfer.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Five-LLM controlled experiment described in the publisher abstract.
eligibility.rationale: Direct prompt mitigation, but decisive full-text methods and effects were inaccessible.

candidates.title: From Single to Societal: Analyzing Persona-Induced Bias in Multi-Agent Interactions

peer_review_evidence.basis: Official AAAI 2026 proceedings record.

eligibility.technical: Controlled persona assignment in collaborative, problem-solving, and persuasion interactions.
eligibility.social: Examines gender, race, trust, insistence, and in-group conformity in multi-agent groups.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: Controlled multi-agent experiments find systematic persona-conditioned interaction effects.
eligibility.rationale: Relevant persona-bias mechanism, but no evaluated mitigation and indirect Human Services transfer.

candidates.title: Implicit Bias in Large Language Model Diagnosis of Eating Disorders: Experimental Vignette Study (Preprint)

preferred_version.reason: Only documented Version by the cutoff.

peer_review_evidence.basis: Title and record explicitly identify a Preprint; no accepted Version located.

eligibility.technical: Matched-pair clinical prompts vary demographic attributes while holding symptoms constant.
eligibility.social: Direct eating-disorder diagnosis, gender, race or ethnicity, age, socioeconomic status, language proficiency, and urbanicity.
eligibility.empirical_evidence: 1,152 synthetic vignettes and ten LLM configurations; large differential diagnostic odds are reported for several groups.
eligibility.rationale: Strong mental-health prompt audit, but no mitigation and unreviewed status place it in Tier B.

notes: A protected full text was not downloaded.

exclusions.title: Effective prompt design for large language models in clinical practice
exclusions.reason: Prompt-design guidance for clinical practice, but no substantive gender, social-bias, inequality, stigma, diversity, or fairness evaluation was established from the publisher metadata.

exclusions.title: Algorithmic bias in clinical resource allocation by a large language model: a cross-sectional in-silico evaluation of 13,608 decisions
exclusions.reason: Strong demographic fairness audit in clinical allocation, but it uses a single zero-shot prompt and does not compare prompt designs, fairness instructions, personas, or prompt mitigation.

exclusions.title: Impact of prompt engineering on large language models for risk of bias assessment: a comparative study
exclusions.reason: The target is methodological risk-of-bias assessment for research studies, not demographic or social bias in LLM behavior; no substantive inequality dimension was established.

exclusions.title: Hedging and Non-Affirmation: Quantifying LLM Alignment on Questions of Human Rights
exclusions.reason: Substantive human-rights bias evidence, but the effective mitigation is activation steering and orthogonalization rather than prompting; it was already recorded in the contextual lane.

exclusions.title: New model, old risks: sociodemographic bias and adversarial hallucinations vulnerability in GPT-5
exclusions.reason: The tested mitigation prompt targets adversarial hallucination, while the sociodemographic bias findings are not mitigated by a prompt intervention.

exclusions.title: Prompt Engineering Limitations: Preliminary Evaluation of Large Language Models for Psychotherapy Safety
exclusions.reason: Unreviewed preliminary psychotherapy-safety study; the available record did not establish a substantive gender, protected-group, inequality, or fairness comparison.

exclusions.title: A clinically validated framework for auditing AI chatbot behavior in mental health interactions
exclusions.reason: Direct mental-health audit with prompt-robustness checks, but demographic and intersectional diversity is a stated limitation rather than an evaluated inequality dimension.

exclusions.title: Between Help and Harm: An Evaluation Study of Mental Health Crisis Handling by LLMs
exclusions.reason: Mental-health crisis evaluation without an established gender, social-bias, inequality, fairness-instruction, or mitigation comparison.

exclusions.title: Operationalizing Pluralistic Values in LLM Alignment Reveals Trade-offs Between Group Fairness and Accuracy
exclusions.reason: Strong demographic fairness study, but the intervention is preference alignment and fine-tuning rather than prompt design or prompt-based mitigation.

exclusions.title: When Consistency Becomes Bias: Interviewer Effects in Semi-Structured Clinical Interviews
exclusions.reason: Important depression-detection artifact study, but interviewer prompts are features in training data rather than prompts to a generative LLM or prompt interventions.

exclusions.reason: Persona-based agents address caste hate-speech classification performance, but the study does not evaluate bias or fairness in model outputs or a debiasing intervention.

exclusions.title: Insights from Multilingual Gender Inclusive Language Generation Shared Task
exclusions.reason: Gender-inclusive rewriting shared-task overview; no distinct prompt-engineering or prompt-effect study was established for the overview paper.
